Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 109, verse 1:

Surat al-Kafirun

Meccan, and its number of verses is six.

﴿Say: O you who disbelieve.﴾ They are specific disbelievers, about whom Allah the Exalted has known that faith will never come from them. It is narrated that a group of the stubborn leaders of Quraysh said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Come, follow our religion and we will follow your religion. You worship our gods for one year, and we will worship your God for one year." He said: "I seek refuge in Allah from associating anything with Him." They said: "Then touch some of our gods, and we will believe you and worship your God." So this was revealed. He went out to the Sacred Mosque, where the chiefs of Quraysh were gathered, stood over their heads and recited it to them, and they despaired.

"I do not worship what you worship" — meaning: in the future. Because "lā" (not) generally enters only upon a present-tense verb referring to the future, just as "mā" (what) enters only upon a present-tense verb referring to the present time. The meaning is: I will not do in the future what you ask of me, namely worshipping your gods.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 109, verse 3:

﴿Nor are you worshippers of what I worship.﴾ That is: nor are you doing in it (i.e., in the worship of my Lord) what I seek from you of worship of my God.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 109, verse 4:

﴿And I will not worship what you worship.﴾ That is: "And I have never been a worshipper, in the past, of what you have worshipped," i.e., there was never known from me the worship of an idol in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam). So how could it be expected of me in Islam?!

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 109, verse 5:

﴿Nor will you worship what I worship.﴾ That is: you have not worshipped, at any time, what I am devoted to worshipping. It has also been said: these two sentences negate worship in the present (ḥālan), just as the first two negate it in the future (istiqbālan). The reason he did not say "what I have worshipped" (mā ʿabadtu) to match "what you have worshipped" (mā ʿabadtum) is that they were marked, before the mission (al-baʿthah), by the worship of idols, whereas he, upon him peace, was not then marked by the worship of God Most High. The choice of "mā" with "aʿbudu" over "man" is because the intended meaning is the attribute, as if it were said: "what I worship" is of the Great Worshipped One, whose greatness cannot be measured. It has also been said that "mā" is verbal-masdarial (maṣdariyyah), meaning: I do not worship your worship, and you do not worship my worship. It has been said: the first two are in the sense of "alladhī" (that which), and the latter two are masdarial. It has also been said: the words of the Most High, ﴿Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped﴾, are an emphasis of the words of the Most High, ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾, and the words of the Most High, ﴿Nor will you worship what I worship﴾, secondly, are an emphasis of their like mentioned first.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 109, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For you is your religion﴾ is a confirmation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped﴾, and just as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and for me is my religion﴾ is a confirmation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾. The meaning is: your religion, which is polytheism (shirk), is restricted to being attained by you alone; it does not extend to being attained by me as well, as you hope for it. So do not attach your empty wishes to it, for that is among the impossibilities. And my religion, which is monotheism (tawhid), is restricted to being attained by me alone; it does not extend to being attained by you as well, because you have tied it to the impossibility, which is your worshipping of my gods or my touching them (istilam). And because what you promised is the very essence of polytheism. Since the basis of their saying, "You worship our gods for one year and we worship your God for one year," was the sharing of both groups in both acts of worship, the restriction derived from placing the predicate first was necessarily a restriction of exclusion (qasr ifrad). It is also possible that this is a confirmation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped﴾, meaning: and for me is my religion, not your religion, as is the case in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and for you is what you have earned﴾. It has been said: the meaning is that I am a prophet sent to you to call you to the truth and salvation. So when you do not accept from me and do not follow me, then leave me alone, and do not call me to polytheism. Reflect on this. From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites from Surat al-Kafirun, it is as if he has recited a quarter of the Qur'an, the rebellious devils keep far from him, he is cleared of shirk, and he is protected from the greatest terror."
